holidays.name: National Chocolate-Covered Cashews Day
holidays.description: Today is for the snack that combines a buttery, crunchy nut with a coat of smooth chocolate. Eat some straight from the bag, toss them into trail mix, or give them to a friend who has earned a treat.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial snack-food observance. Its origins are unclear, but it has become a regular fixture on the April calendar of food holidays.
holidays.funFact: Cashews grow attached to the bottom of a fruit called the cashew apple. The shell around each nut contains an irritating oil related to the one in poison ivy, so cashews are never sold in the shell.

holidays.name: Bulldogs Are Beautiful Day
holidays.description: This day celebrates the wrinkly, droopy-jowled, snorting charm of bulldogs. Whether you own an English bulldog, a French bulldog or an American bulldog, it's a day to admire their squished faces and stubborn personalities.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial pet-appreciation observance of unclear origin. Bulldog fans keep it going, and it's popular on social media.
holidays.funFact: Bulldogs were originally bred in England for bull-baiting, a cruel sport banned in 1835. Breeders later developed the gentle, couch-loving companions we know today.

holidays.name: National Kindergarten Day
holidays.description: This day honors the first stepping stone of school, with finger paints, circle time, nap mats and learning through play. It's an excuse to remember your own kindergarten days and thank the teachers who made them fun.
holidays.origin: The date marks the birthday of Friedrich Froebel, who was born on April 21, 1782. The German educator founded the first kindergarten in 1837.
holidays.funFact: Kindergarten is German for 'children's garden'. Froebel chose the name because he thought children should be nurtured and allowed to grow like plants.
